title: Reflow safeguards for dashboard panels and modal overlaps
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Problem: Multiple console pages (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) show unpredictable layout reflows and element overlap at intermediate widths and on legacy browsers (EdgeHTML/older Safari). Charts and table headers can clip or become inaccessible when modals open on top of complex grid panels. This leads to visual regressions and occasional loss of keyboard focus/accessibility order.
goals: 1) Create resilient grid and stacking rules to prevent panel clipping and modal overlap across breakpoints. 2) Ensure consistent table header stickiness and chart axis visibility at common widths and DPRs. 3) Provide documented CSS fallbacks for legacy browsers and feature-detected polyfills where necessary. 4) Deliver Figma prototypes and cross-browser QA checklist for engineering handoff.
success_metrics: Reduction in cross-browser visual regressions reported by QA from >6/week to <=1/week; no high-severity layout regressions in the next two releases; automated Percy visual diffs for 6 canonical viewports pass in CI.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Dashboard grid uses containment-aware reflow strategy so panels never overlap modals. 2) Tables maintain header visibility and horizontal scrolling without clipped controls at widths 320px, 480px, 768px, 1024px, 1366px. 3) Charts keep axis labels visible with a compact mode that switches at <=480px. 4) Cross-browser stylesheet includes documented fallbacks for Edge (legacy), Safari 13+, and Firefox ESR. 5) Design tokens and spacing variables are used; no magic pixel shifts introduced.
design_work_done:
- Interactive Figma prototype: dashboard reflow variants (desktop, tablet, narrow-tablet, mobile compact). Link: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/reflow-safeguards-DES-12015 (internal).
- Component sketches for Panel, Modal, TableHeader, ChartCompactMode.
- CSS module spec with containment (contain: layout/content) recommendations and z-index scale.
- Accessibility notes: preserve tabindex ordering, ensure focus trap in modals, provide ARIA announcements when chart layout changes.
engineering_notes: Proposed implementation options evaluated with Eng: 1) CSS Grid with subgrid fallback + JS resize observer shim for legacy browsers; 2) Flexbox fallback with explicit collapse behavior; 3) Absolute-positioned modal layers with compaction heuristics. Eng prefers Grid + ResizeObserver plus a minimal polyfill for Edge legacy. We agreed on token-driven spacing and a shared utility class for stacking context.
qa_matrix: Browsers: Chrome 120 (win/mac), Firefox 115 (win/mac), Safari 15+, Safari 13 (macOS Mojave), Edge Chromium latest, Edge Legacy (where supported)
High-DPI: 2x DPR checks on macOS and Android emulation
Assistive tech: VoiceOver and NVDA smoke tests for modal focus and table navigation
test_steps: Open Dashboards > Cost Overview in each viewport and confirm panels do not overlap when opening 'Create Alert' modal.
Resize from 1366 -> 1024 -> 768 -> 480 -> 320 and observe no clipped chart axes; compact chart mode should enable at <=480.
Trigger keyboard-only modal open (Enter on button) and tab through to confirm focus trap and return focus on close.
Run Percy visual snapshot job with 6 canonical viewports and attach diffs to the PR.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Using ResizeObserver introduces runtime cost; mitigated by debounce and only enabling shims on legacy browsers.
- Subgrid fallback increases CSS complexity; tradeoff accepted for fewer JS layout fixes.
- Slight visual differences in compact chart labels on older Safari; added copy-level notes in design tokens.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge CSS + small JS shim behind feature flag. 2) Enable for 10% of users on Canary deployment using runtime flag. 3) Monitor Percy and SLO dashboards for visual regressions and UX errors. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% after 7 days without regressions.
